blocks.html:
Retrieves the authenticated actor's resolved permission set: a flat list
of `resource:operation` strings with wildcards already expanded, along
with the actor's assigned roles and the names of the roles the actor's
permissions fully cover.

```ts
sdk.admin.rbacRole.mePermissions()
.then(({ permissions, roles, covered_roles }) => {
  console.log(permissions) // ["product:read", "customer:read", ...]
  console.log(roles) // [{ id: "role_123", name: "Product Manager" }]
  console.log(covered_roles) // ["Product Manager", "Product Reader"]
})
```

types.name: query
types.description: The scope to resolve the permissions within.

children.name: scope
children.description:
The type of the scope to resolve the permissions within. Only takes
effect together with `scope_id`; otherwise the request's ambient scope
applies.

children.name: scope_id
children.description:
The ID of the scope to resolve the permissions within. Only takes effect
together with `scope`.

types.description: Headers to pass in the request.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The flat permission list, assigned roles, and covered role names.

children.name: permissions
children.description: The actor's effective `resource:operation` permissions, with wildcards already expanded.

children.name: roles
children.description: The actor's directly assigned roles, considering the resolved scope.

children.name: covered_roles
children.description:
Names of the roles the actor covers: roles whose grants are a subset of
the actor's effective permissions. Assigned roles are always covered, and
a super admin covers every role. Roles without policies are covered by
no one.
